rules.problem: One of the nine red-box danger signs is missing: 'Hb < 12 (woman) or < 13 (man)'. The grammar has no sex and no g/dL unit, so it cannot be encoded literally, but it was dropped silently rather than approximated; the closest proxy is (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Anemia" "disorder")) (exists), added to the or and to the task's check_for. Type, Urgent level ('Refer urgently'), trigger and and/or structure are otherwise faithful.

summary: The urgent priority rule and its check_for task silently omit one of the nine red-box danger signs, 'Hb < 12 (woman) or < 13 (man)'; the grammar cannot express sex or g/dL, but an Anemia proxy exists and should be added so a jaundiced anaemic patient is not missed. Everything else encoded is on the page and every SNOMED concept resolves; the remaining issues are precision only: the tinea versicolor dark-patch branch is pinned to the trunk although the page says 'usually on trunk, neck and upper arms', White hair is narrower than 'involves hair', Acute confusion adds acuity the page does not state (and is redundant with Clouded consciousness), and the '≥ 4 drinks/session' binge threshold is dropped. Not invented but worth noting as page content left unencoded: 'Patient has acute hepatitis A infection' on a positive hepatitis A IgM (closest concept (snomed_concept "Acute type A viral hepatitis" "disorder")) and the 2-day review referral thresholds (ALT ≥ 200, INR ≥ 1.5, plts < 150).
